# NVDA (NVIDIA Corporation — NMS, Technology/Semiconductors)
## Technical Deep-Dive — Analysis date: 2026-11-11 (close)

---

## 1. Executive Summary

NVDA is in a **confirmed intermediate downtrend that has just produced a short-term capitulation signature**. From the 2026-10-06 close of **239.24** to the 2026-11-11 close of **173.73**, the stock has lost **65.51 points, or −27.4%** — and the 2026-10-06 intraday high of **243.37** to the 2026-11-10 intraday low of **165.89** is **−31.8%**. Price now sits **below all three major moving averages** (10 EMA 188.57, 50 SMA 217.10, 200 SMA 204.19), **14.9% below the 200-day**, with **RSI at 28.74** and a **Bollinger 2-sigma lower band tag-and-reject** on 2026-11-10/11.

That is a violently oversold condition — but critically, **there is no confirmed reversal signal yet**. Momentum (MACD line still making new lows at **−12.12**), the absence of a bullish RSI divergence, and the still-negative structure (price < 50 SMA < ... but 50 > 200) all say the *trend* is down. The 2026-11-09/11-11 tape (three sessions totalling ~1.16B shares vs a ~162M/day 20-day average) is a **climax-volume event**, which historically marks *zones* of exhaustion, not precise bottoms. The tradable conclusion: **oversold-bounce risk/reward is improving for nimble tactical longs, but the strategic trend is broken and rallies into 188–189 and 203–204 should be treated as supply until proven otherwise.**

---

## 2. Price Structure and Trend

### The breakdown sequence (all values from verified tool output)

|---|---:|---|
| 2026-10-06 | 239.24 | Cycle peak close (intraday high 243.37 same day) |
| 2026-10-29 | 213.66 | Loss of the Sept–Oct 210–220 shelf begins |
| 2026-10-30 | 204.64 | Closed *at* the 200 SMA (204.09) — last stand |

| 2026-11-09 | 178.67 | Gap down to 173.07 open; low 170.24; record volume 462.7M |

| 2026-11-11 | 173.73 | Recovered inside the band; close +2.9% vs 2026-11-10 |

The **2026-11-11 close of 173.73 is the lowest close in the dataset since 2026-03-30 (164.79)** — i.e., roughly 7.5 months of gains have been surrendered. The 2026-11-10 low of **165.89** effectively tagged the 2026-03-30 close of **164.79**, the last visible consolidation floor in the series. That 164.79–165.89 zone is the single most important structural line on the chart.

### Moving averages — a fully bearish stack, with a death cross forming

- **10 EMA = 188.57**: price is **7.9% below** it and the EMA is collapsing (−3.30 per session on 2026-11-10 → 2026-11-11, from 230.71 on 2026-10-12). This is the first meaningful overhead pivot.
- **50 SMA = 217.10**: rolling over decisively (222.46 on 2026-10-12 → 217.10 on 2026-11-11; recent pace ≈ −0.87/session). Price is **20.0% below** it.
- **200 SMA = 204.19**: price is **14.9% below** it. More importantly, the 200 SMA has just **stopped rising**: it climbed from 202.02 (2026-10-12) to a peak of **204.39 on 2026-11-06**, and has now ticked down two consecutive sessions (204.26 → 204.19). The long-term trend benchmark is flattening/rolling — a strategic warning, not a tactical one.
- **50/200 spread = +12.91 points (6.3%)**, down from **+20.44 points (10.1%)** on 2026-10-12. At the current convergence pace (~0.82 points/session) a **death cross would arrive around early-to-mid December 2026** if the decline persists. Frame this as a *projection under current slope*, not a forecast.

**Interpretation:** The golden-cross regime (50 > 200) is technically still intact, which is why this still reads as a *deep correction inside a longer uptrend* rather than a completed bear market. But the price has already invalidated that uptrend by trading 14.9% under its own 200-day benchmark. In practice, the 50/200 cross is a lagging formality — the actionable damage is already done.

---

## 3. Momentum

**RSI (14) = 28.74.** The path: 52.03 (2026-10-13) → 46.31 (2026-10-27) → 35.07 (2026-10-30) → **25.40 (2026-11-05)** → 30.77 (2026-11-06) → 27.41 (2026-11-09) → **23.95 (2026-11-10, the period low)** → **28.74 (2026-11-11)**.

Three nuances matter more than the raw "oversold" label:

1. **This is a persistent, grinding oversold — not a one-day flush.** Four of the last five sessions closed below 30. Oversold readings that persist indicate *seller control*, not imminent reversal.
2. **No bullish divergence.** RSI made a *lower low* (23.95) on 2026-11-10 alongside a *lower close* (168.89). Momentum has not yet refused to confirm price — the single most reliable early reversal tell is absent.
3. **The stock never got overbought on the way up.** RSI peaked at only ~52 in mid-October. The decline began from neutral momentum, meaning there was no momentum "exhaustion" to unwind — which argues this was a *repricing*, not a froth blow-off, and repricings can extend.

**MACD = −12.12, Signal = −8.03, Histogram = −4.09.** The MACD line crossed below its signal on **2026-10-22** (MACD −1.98 vs signal +0.07) and has been negative ever since. The histogram's decline was interrupted by a mild improvement into 2026-10-29 (−1.03), then **re-deteriorated to its worst reading of the entire move at −4.28 on 2026-11-10**, ticking back to −4.09 on 2026-11-11. Note the split message: the **histogram improved marginally on 2026-11-11 while the MACD line itself made a new low (−12.12 vs −11.29)** — the classic "downside acceleration losing steam but trend still down" configuration. Confirmation of a bottom requires the histogram to turn positive or at minimum build a sustained two-week sequence of higher lows.

---

## 4. Volatility — the story of this decline

**ATR = 8.70**, equal to **5.0% of the 173.73 close**. ATR has expanded **+55.6%** from 5.59 on 2026-10-13. This is not a normal-volatility pullback; it is a re-rating.

**Bollinger Bands (20, 2):** Mid **203.80**, Upper **236.97**, Lower **170.64**.
- Bandwidth = (236.97 − 170.64) / 203.80 = **32.5%**, versus ~12.6% implied on 2026-10-12 (upper 241.80, lower 213.21, mid 227.50) — a **~2.6x expansion** in two months.
- **%B = 0.047** — price is pinned to the very bottom of the envelope, just **1.8% above the lower band**.
- **2026-11-10 closed 3.7% *below* the lower band** (168.89 vs 175.36) and **2026-11-11 snapped back inside** (173.73 vs 170.64). A one-session close outside a 2-sigma band that immediately reverses is a textbook **failed-breakdown / exhaustion wick** — but it requires follow-through above 177.54 (2026-11-11 high) and then 181.60 (2026-11-05 close) to become actionable.
- Because the bands are so wide, **the lower band is a moving target that is rising fast** (175.36 → 170.64 in one session it *fell*, i.e., the band is catching down to price, not acting as support). Do not treat 170.64 as a floor; treat it as a volatility marker.

**Risk implication:** with ATR at 8.70, a "1-ATR stop" is 5% and a conventional 1.5–2 ATR stop is **7.5–10%**. Position size must be cut proportionally — roughly **half to two-thirds of normal** for the same dollar risk budget.

---

## 5. Volume — the most compelling evidence

**VWMA = 189.15**, down from 231.55 on 2026-10-12. The volume-weighted average price of the last ~30 sessions sits **8.1% above spot**, and it is falling ~1.5 points/day. This tells us the decline has occurred **on heavy volume, with institutions transacting at higher prices** — a large, recently-underwater buyer cohort now represents overhead supply. Note also that **VWMA (189.15) and the 10 EMA (188.57) converge at ~188–189** — a highly reliable "value area" pivot.

Volume details from the tape:
- **2026-11-09: 462.7M shares — the highest volume print in the entire 386-session dataset** (previous high 369.2M on 2025-05-29), a **~2.9x** multiple of the ~162M 20-day average (derived from the last 20 sessions in the tool output).
- **2026-11-10: 429.3M (~2.7x average)**; **2026-11-11: 266.6M (~1.65x average)**.
- Three-session total ≈ **1.16 billion shares**.

Reading the intraday closes relative to each day's range: 2026-11-09 closed at **87% of its range** (178.67 within 170.24–179.92) = aggressive dip buying; 2026-11-10 closed at **34%** of range (168.89 within 165.89–174.69) = renewed supply; 2026-11-11 closed at **44%** of range (173.73 within 170.77–177.54) = balanced, slight recovery. The **declining volume into the 2026-11-11 bounce is a caution** — real bottoms typically show *expanding* volume on the reversal day.

**Verdict on volume:** this is a distribution-then-capitulation sequence. The heaviest volume of the year printed at the lows, which is behaviorally consistent with a *selling climax*, but the lack of a high-volume up-day means **demand has not yet been proven**.

---

---

## 7. Scenarios and Actionable Playbook

**Scenario A — Oversold bounce / mean reversion (probability-weighted as the near-term base case).**
Trigger: a daily close above **177.54**, ideally above **181.60** with volume > 266M. Objectives: **188.5–189.1** (10 EMA/VWMA confluence) first, then **203.8–204.2** (Bollinger mid + 200 SMA). Tactical long framework: entry 168–174, stop below **165.50** (under the 2026-11-10 low), risk ≈ 8.2 points from spot; reward to 188.5 ≈ 14.8 points (**1.8:1**), to 204 ≈ 30.3 points (**3.7:1**). Size at 50–65% of normal because 1 ATR alone is 5%.

**Scenario B — Bear continuation (needs to be respected).**
Trigger: a daily close below **165.89**, or a rejection candle at 188–189 on heavy volume. That opens the **164.79** area and leaves no tool-verified support below it in the dataset. Trend-followers should remain short-biased/underweight while price is under the 200 SMA (204.19), but note the asymmetry: shorting a −27% move with RSI at 28.7 is poor reward-to-risk *at spot*; the higher-quality short entry is a failed retest of **188–204**, not here.

**Scenario C — Trend repair (low probability near term).**
Requires: reclaim of **204.19** (200 SMA), MACD histogram turning positive, and RSI recovering above 50 while the 50 SMA holds above the 200 SMA. Until then, every rally is a counter-trend move inside a broken structure.

**Invalidation / stop discipline:** the 2026-11-10 low of **165.89** is the line that separates "oversold bounce" from "structural breakdown." Any long must be defined against it.

---

## 8. Why These 8 Indicators

| Indicator | Value (2026-11-11) | Why it earns a slot here |

| **macdh** | −4.09 | Encodes the MACD/signal relationship and spot the first inflection (it ticked up on 2026-11-11 while MACD made a new low) — the earliest momentum tell |

| **close_50_sma** | 217.10 | Medium-term trend + the death-cross geometry (spread compressing from 20.44 to 12.91) |
| **boll_lb** | 170.64 | Quantifies the 2-sigma stretch; the 2026-11-10 close below it and 2026-11-11 recovery is the exhaustion signal |
| **atr** | 8.70 | Volatility has expanded 55.6%; it is the sizing and stop engine (5% of price) |
| **vwma** | 189.15 | Volume-weighted truth: the decline is volume-backed, and 189.15 marks the overhead supply/value area |

*Deliberately excluded:* **close_10_ema** (188.57) — it is within 0.6 points of VWMA (189.15), so VWMA was retained because it carries the same level **plus** volume weighting; the 10 EMA value is still cited as confluence. **boll** (203.80) was excluded as near-duplicate of the 200 SMA (204.19). **macds** was excluded because the histogram conveys the same information more directly. **boll_ub** was excluded as irrelevant while price is pinned to the floor.

---

## 9. Bottom Line

NVDA is a **broken intermediate uptrend sitting on a capitulation low**. The evidence for a tradeable bounce is real — RSI 28.7, a close outside and immediate recovery back inside the lower Bollinger Band, the highest volume print in 386 sessions, and price within 5% of the last structural floor (164.79–165.89). The evidence against trusting it is equally real — no RSI divergence, MACD making fresh lows, price 14.9% under the 200 SMA with the 200 SMA itself rolling over, a death cross ~3–4 weeks away on current slope, and a bounce on *declining* volume. **Trade the bounce small and defined; do not confuse an oversold condition with a new uptrend. 188–189 is where the answer arrives.**

## NVDA Sentiment Report — 2026-11-04 → 2026-11-11

**Bottom line up front:** the only live source this week is StockTwits, and it leans modestly bullish (roughly 5–6 bullish vs. 2 bearish out of 20 on-topic posts) — but the lean is shallow, earnings-anticipation-driven, and heavily contaminated by off-topic chatter about a Jensen Huang personal-conduct story. With the news feed and Reddit both returning hard failures, this is a **low-confidence, single-source read**. Treat it as a sentiment temperature check, not a directional trade signal.

---

### 1. Source-by-source breakdown

**Yahoo Finance news — DATA UNAVAILABLE (no observations).**
The feed returned `YFDataException`; no configured vendor could serve `get_news`. This is a vendor outage, **not** evidence of silence around NVDA. Consequence: I have **no institutional framing** for the week — no confirmation or denial of the governance/personal-conduct story that dominates retail chatter, no earnings-date or guidance commentary, and no way to weigh event-driven headlines. Any institutional-vs-retail divergence test (the highest-value cross-check available to a sentiment analyst) is **impossible this cycle**.

**Reddit (r/wallstreetbets, r/stocks, r/investing) — UNAVAILABLE (fetch failed).**
Placeholder, explicitly "not an absence of discussion." I therefore cannot gauge the retail *community* layer — where r/wallstreetbets would normally give the exuberant/contrarian read and r/stocks/r/investing the measured, longer-horizon read. No post bodies, no themes, no engagement inference (and per method, I would not infer engagement from titles anyway).

**StockTwits — 20 on-topic NVDA posts (30 fetched, 20 screened as NVDA-relevant).**
Classifier stance count: **6 bullish / 2 bearish / 5 neutral / 7 unclear**. The feed header's own tally reads **Bullish 5 (25%) / Bearish 2 (10%) / Unlabeled 13 (65%)** — a one-post discrepancy between the two tallies on the bullish line. Either way, the honest description is: **bulls outnumber bears roughly 2.5–3:1, but ~65% of posts carry no directional label at all**, so the ratio is computed on a small labeled subset (~7–8 posts) and should be treated as soft.

Two material data-quality caveats beyond sample size:

- **Time compression.** Every timestamp falls between 2026-11-11T21:33Z and 21:46Z — a **~13-minute burst**, not a seven-day distribution. This is a single-snapshot sentiment reading on one afternoon, not a trend. There is no way to see whether sentiment built, faded, or reversed over the week.
- **Topic contamination.** A large share of the 13 unlabeled posts are not about the stock at all: memes and links (@HydrogenH2 ×2 YouTube links, @Bears_be_gone "fake hit / fake ICU scene", @Monse_Trades "Jensen is the $SPY"), open questions (@Andy09999 "call or put?", @Carlos_trades "what's everybody's short-term price target"), and one post tagged `$NVDA` that is substantively about **$ORCL** (@unassuming). Adjusting for that, the *effective* directional sample is closer to a dozen posts.

**What the bulls actually said (and how strong it is):**
- @OnlyBuysDips (Bullish): "$200+ after a blowout earnings beat" — clean, explicit, but 100% conditional on an event that has not happened.
- @escuintla (no-label, directionally bullish): "if good earnings $200 +" — same conditional structure.
- @Stockolert (Bullish): "more likely to beat earnings than miss them. In the meantime, we're fucked until they release the earnings early" — bullish on the event, impatient/bearish on the intervening tape.
- @Zaldiar365 (Bullish): relief trade — "felt really bad that micron and dell went upside like 15% today (finished 12%) and nvda only 3.2% but at least its not dropping." This is **relative-value frustration dressed as bullishness**, and it is one of the few concrete price facts in the dataset: NVDA reportedly +3.2% on the day while Micron and Dell reportedly +12–15%.
- @PrimedUp (Bullish): the bullish tag is incidental — the body is a defense of Jensen Huang over the affair/spy story.

**What the bears actually said (and how strong it is):**
- @stockit111 (Bearish): "Nothing too big to fail, NOTHING!" + an Apple News link — a governance/headline-risk bear case, but with no articulated thesis.
- @Ozyil (Bearish): "im broke, i buy at 0.01 cent" — either sarcasm, a joke about a penny-stock scenario, or a garbled post. **Not usable as evidence of a bearish thesis.**

So: the bear side is essentially one link-drop and one joke. The bull side is essentially one repeated conditional ("$200 if earnings beat"). Neither side has a developed argument in this sample.

**Genuinely informative posts (direction-agnostic but useful):**
- @funkymonkey_ : "shorting at these levels with earnings next week a risky play" — implies **earnings are ~one week out** and flags asymmetric event risk for shorts.
- @TopOptionsAIerts : "That target math is the tell. 500 to 200 is an opinion changing, not $NVDA changing. Price into the close matters more than the headline." — a pushback against headline-driven target revisions; reads as a discipline/anti-hype voice.
- @Itsokman : "I sense indecision" — consistent with the 65% unlabeled share.

---

### 2. Cross-source divergences and alignments

**Not assessable in the normal sense.** Cross-source divergence analysis requires at least two substantive sources; I have one. Specifically, the classic high-value pattern — *retail bullish while institutional framing is cautious, or vice versa* — **cannot be tested this week**, and I will not guess at what the news flow "probably" said.

What I can say is that the data has an internal divergence worth naming: **retail is bullish on the event but not on the tape.** The same posters who expect a beat also describe waiting ("we're fucked until they release the earnings early"), note NVDA lagging Micron/Dell badly on the day, and call the setup "indecision." That is *anticipatory* bullishness with no current-momentum confirmation behind it — conviction borrowed against a future catalyst rather than earned from price action. Anticipatory bullishness ahead of a binary event is the pattern most prone to sharp reversal if the event disappoints.

The second internal divergence is thematic: the **single largest cluster of posts is not about the business at all** — it is about an alleged Jensen Huang affair and a spying/blackmail storyline. Retail is split on interpretation (@PrimedUp, @Lateralus1 "Jense was blackmailed… awfully sus that this story is years old and comes out now", @sharetp02 "Jensen was cleared of any wrongdoings. He was a target", @MontgomeryB, and a call-for-resignation prompt referenced via @sharetp02's reply to @StocktwitsPolls). This is a **key-person / governance narrative** running in parallel with the earnings narrative, and sentiment on it is defensive-to-dismissive rather than panicked.

---

### 3. Dominant narrative themes

1. **Earnings as the only catalyst that matters (dominant).** Referenced repeatedly as "next week." The bull case is entirely event-conditional and clustered at a "$200+" round-number target. Two distinct sub-frames: (a) probability edge — "more likely to beat than miss"; (b) impatience — the stock is seen as marking time until the print.
2. **Key-person / governance risk around Jensen Huang.** An affair-plus-espionage storyline is circulating; retail response is largely defensive (blackmail theory, "no proof," "he was cleared"). Note the asymmetry: retail is *discounting* this risk, which means if it escalates into something institutional (board, legal, disclosure), it is **not priced by this crowd**.
3. **Relative underperformance vs. semis peers.** NVDA +3.2% vs. Micron ~+12% and Dell ~+15% on the same day, per one poster. Frames NVDA as the laggard in an up semis tape — a mild "why aren't we participating?" grievance.
4. **Event-risk asymmetry for shorts.** Explicit view that shorting into the print is a bad risk/reward — a soft bullish tell.
5. **Round-number anchoring / target inflation.** "$200," "$200+," "500 to 200" all appear; one poster explicitly calls out target math as an unreliable tell. Round-number anchoring is a classic sign of narrative-driven rather than valuation-driven positioning.

---

### 4. Catalysts and risks surfaced by the data

**Catalysts**
- **NVDA earnings ~one week out** (per multiple posts). The entire bullish lean is levered to this binary. Expect sentiment to stay event-anchored and gamma-like until the print.
- **Peer strength in semis/hardware** (Micron, Dell reportedly +12–15% on the day) — a supportive read-through if it persists, and a source of relative-value flows into NVDA.

**Risks**
- **Headline/governance risk from the Huang storyline.** Retail is dismissing it; that dismissal is itself the risk, because it implies under-pricing if the story develops legs (board action, resignation pressure, disclosure, or confirmation of a security incident).
- **Conditional-bullishness unwind.** If earnings land merely in line, the "$200+" crowd has no fallback thesis in this dataset — sentiment could flip fast and loudly.
- **Relative-laggard frustration.** Continued peer outperformance without NVDA participation tends to convert bulls into momentum defectors.
- **Short-squeeze-in-reverse / positioning ambiguity.** Nobody in the sample expresses a clear bearish thesis, which means bearish conviction (if it exists) is not visible here — a blind spot.

---

### 5. Key sentiment signals

| Signal | Direction | Source | Supporting evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Retail stance skew on NVDA | Mildly Bullish | StockTwits (20 on-topic posts) | ~5–6 bullish vs 2 bearish; but 13/20 unlabeled (65%), so ratio rests on ~7–8 labeled posts |
| Earnings anticipation | Bullish (speculative, event-conditional) | StockTwits | "@OnlyBuysDips: $200+ after a blowout earnings beat"; "@escuintla: if good earnings $200+"; "@Stockolert: more likely to beat than miss" |
| Key-person / governance storyline (Huang affair/spy allegations) | Bearish risk, currently *discounted* by retail | StockTwits | 5+ posts debating the story; "@Lateralus1: Jense was blackmailed"; "@sharetp02: NO PROOF… he was cleared"; resignation prompt referenced |
| Relative underperformance vs. semis peers | Mildly Bearish (internal) | StockTwits | "@Zaldiar365: micron and dell went upside like 15%… nvda only 3.2% but at least its not dropping" |
| Event-risk asymmetry for shorts | Mildly Bullish | StockTwits | "@funkymonkey_: shorting at these levels with earnings next week a risky play" |
| Anti-hype / discipline voices | Neutral | StockTwits | "@TopOptionsAIerts: 500 to 200 is an opinion changing… Price into the close matters more than the headline"; "@Itsokman: I sense indecision" |
| Institutional framing | **Unavailable** | Yahoo Finance news | `YFDataException` — vendor failure, not instrument silence |
| Community discussion | **Unavailable** | Reddit (WSB/stocks/investing) | fetch failed — explicitly "not an absence of discussion" |

---

### 6. Confidence and data-quality statement

**Confidence: LOW.** Two of three sources returned placeholders; the surviving source is (a) small (20 on-topic posts, ~7–8 carrying a directional label), (b) compressed into a **~13-minute window** rather than spread across the 7-day period, (c) ~65% unlabeled, and (d) significantly off-topic (memes, links, cross-ticker `$ORCL` drift, one likely-sarcastic bearish tag). The internal snapshot tallies disagree by one post on the bullish count. There is **no institutional leg** to this read and no community-discussion leg, so I cannot claim the ~2.5–3:1 bull/bear tilt is a market-wide phenomenon — only that it is what one retail cashtag stream looked like on the afternoon of 2026-11-11.

**Framing:** this is a sentiment signal to weigh alongside fundamentals, positioning, and technicals — **not a price call**. The most actionable observation is not "retail is bullish" but "retail bullishness is *entirely borrowed against next week's earnings* while simultaneously dismissing a governance headline that institutional investors may not be dismissing."
